channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Euro trims gains against the Japanese Yen but maintains a near-term bullish trend
item.description: The Euro (EUR) pulls back from intra-week highs just above 185.60 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Wednesday but maintains its immediate bullish bias, trading 0.5% higher on the week so far.

item.title: Gold sticks to intraday losses as oil-driven inflation fears lift Fed rate hike odds
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its offered tone through the first half of the European session on Wednesday and remains vulnerable after the previous day's failed attempt to find acceptance above the $4,100 mark.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC seen steady as Oil supports CAD – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole expects the Bank of Canada to keep rates at 2.25%, with limited incentive to push back against modest December tightening pricing. He sees June CPI potentially falling below 3.0% as petrol prices drop, while core remains near 2.0%.

item.title: PBoC’s Deputy Governor: To continue to implement appropriately loose monetary policy
item.description: People’s Bank of China (PBoC) Deputy Governor said during the European trading session on Wednesday that the central bank remains committed to loose monetary policy conditions to support overall demand.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Upside momentum building toward 0.7015 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note AUD/USD surged to 0.6992 after an earlier dip, with strong short-term momentum pointing to further gains. They see scope for a test of 0.6995, while the major resistance at 0.7015 is key.

item.title: GBP/JPY remains close to multi-year peak as UK-Japan rate gap and Iran risks undermine JPY
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross scales higher for the second straight day and climbs to a fresh weekly top, around the 217.70 region, during the first half of the European session on Wednesday.

item.title: Dow Jones futures edge lower as traders weigh on US-Iran tensions
item.description: Dow Jones futures inch lower by 0.04% to trade around 52,770 during European trading hours on Wednesday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq 100 futures advance 0.19% and 0.79%, trading near 7,600 and 30,030, respectively.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Inflation scenarios guide rate path – ABN AMRO
item.description: ABN AMRO’s Rogier Quaedvlieg reviews the latest United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) downside surprise and its implications for the Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar retreats after soft inflation data, focus shifts to BoC rate decision
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Wednesday, July 15:

item.title: US Dollar: Support pillar weakens after CPI – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes that weaker US CPI has sharply reduced market expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike, undermining a key source of recent US Dollar strength.

item.title: WTI rises to near $79.50 amid intensifying US-Iran hostilities near Hormuz
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price continues to gain ground for the third successive day, trading around $79.40 per barrel during the European session on Wednesday.

item.title: Euro picks up favoured by a weaker US Dollar but remains within previous ranges
item.description: The Euro (EUR) extends gains for the second consecutive day against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, but remains trapped within the trading range seen over the last three weeks, with upside attempts capped below the 1.1470-1.1480 area so far.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ hawkish tone supports gains – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) continues to outperform G10 peers, underpinned by hawkish Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) rhetoric and improving domestic activity data.

item.title: Indian Rupee gains support as traders dial down hawkish Fed bets
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains ground against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday after rising significantly in the last three trading days.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Bulls await breakout above 0.5840-0.5845 confluence on weaker USD
item.description: The NZD/USD pair holds steady above the 0.5800 mark through the early European session on Wednesday and, for now, seems to have stalled the previous day's late pullback from a nearly one-month high, around the 0.5845 zone.

item.title: Brent: Stable prices follow short squeeze – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Michael Every notes Brent Oil holding steady around $85-86 per barrel after an aggressive short squeeze. Every links this stability to ongoing Middle East tensions, United States (US) sanctions enforcement in Hormuz, and strategic efforts to develop alternative pipelines.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Remains below 101.00 near ascending channel bottom
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is extending its losses for the second successive day, trading around 100.80 during the early European hours on Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar strengthens to near 0.7000 as soft US CPI tempers Fed tightening bets
item.description: The AUD/USD pair gathers strength to around 0.6990 during the early European trading hours on Wednesday. The US Dollar (USD) softens against the Australian Dollar (AUD) as markets reduced their bets of a US rate hike after US inflation slowed more than expected in June.

item.title: Euro snaps three-day losing streak against Canadian Dollar, BoC policy eyed
item.description: The Euro (EUR) bounces back against the Canadian Dollar (CAD) after a three-day losing streak, trading 0.13% higher to near 1.6078 during the European trading session on Wednesday.

item.title: British Pound: Advance stalled with neutral range view against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight that GBP/USD’s late-month advance has stalled, with the pair rebounding to 1.3442 before closing at 1.3387. Intraday, the British Pound (GBP) is expected to trade between 1.3360 and 1.3430.

item.title: US Dollar: Long positioning faces reality check – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee warns that speculative long positions in the US Dollar (USD) look vulnerable after June US CPI surprised on the downside.

item.title: Gold: Rebound needs softer Oil and data – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong report that Gold has rebounded from sub-4000 levels after softer United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) prompted markets to pare Fed hike expectations and pushed USD and front-end US Treasury yields lower.

item.title: Silver Price Forecasts: XAG/USD holds below $59.00 despite US Dollar’s weakness
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) ticks lower on Wednesday, trading at $58.50 at the time of writing, after rejection at the $59.00 area on Tuesday. The sour market sentiment amid rising hostilities in Iran continues to weigh on the precious metal, offsetting the positive impact of a weaker US Dollar Index (DXY).

item.title: Equities: CPI-driven gains and tech dispersion – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists note that softer United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI), gains in chipmakers and strong bank earnings supported US equities despite sharp weakness in software stocks.

item.title: Japan's Takaichi: Food inflation has decelerated slightly, but still remains high
item.description: Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Wednesday that food inflation has decelerated slightly but still remains high.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Appreciation scope seen limited against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Volkmar Baur at Commerzbank highlights that China’s weak domestic economy and reliance on exports constrain upside for the Chinese Yuan. Despite solid export growth and sizeable trade surpluses, investment and real retail sales remain soft.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Reflects volatility contraction amid triangle formation
item.description: The USD/JPY pair trades slightly lower at around 162.20 during the European trading session on Wednesday. The pair edges down as the US Dollar (USD) underperforms due to easing fears of interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve (Fed) this year.

item.title: Canadian Dollar edges higher ahead of BoC rate decision
item.description: The USD/CAD pair loses traction to near 1.4050 during the early European trading hours on Wednesday. Traders expect the US Federal Reserve (Fed) to skip the July rate hike as inflation cools, weighing on the US Dollar (USD) against the Canadian Dollar (CAD).

item.title: Euro: Range-trading bias around recent highs against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report EUR/USD briefly spiked to 1.1462 after weaker United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) before retreating to 1.1419.

item.title: Euro edges higher against British Pound as oil surge lifts ECB rate expectations
item.description: The EUR/GBP cross gains momentum to near 0.8535 during the early European trading hours on Wednesday. Traders ramp up bets on the Bank of England (BoE) and European Central Bank (ECB) rate hikes as oil price surge reignites inflation fears.
